What is GST registration? GST registration is the process of enrolling a business under the Goods and Services Tax law to receive a 15-digit GSTIN. It lets you legally collect GST, claim input tax credit and issue tax invoices. Who needs GST registration in India? Businesses crossing ₹40 lakh turnover for goods or ₹20 lakh for services in normal states. Inter-state suppliers, e-commerce sellers, casual taxable persons and reverse charge payers must register regardless of turnover. How many days does GST registration take? Three working days under the Rule 14A scheme, seven working days on the standard Aadhaar-authenticated route, and up to 30 days if flagged for biometric or physical verification. Is GST registration free? Yes. The government charges no fee on gst.gov.in. Professional fees are separate. What is Rule 14A GST registration? Rule 14A is an optional scheme effective from 1 November 2025 granting registration within three working days to applicants whose monthly output tax on B2B supplies stays at or below ₹2.5 lakh, subject to Aadhaar authentication. What happens if I do not register for GST? You owe all the tax you should have collected, plus 18% annual interest, plus a penalty of ₹10,000 or 10% of the tax due, whichever is higher. Deliberate evasion raises it to 100%. Do freelancers need GST registration? Only if annual receipts cross ₹20 lakh in normal states or ₹10 lakh in special category states. Freelancers serving overseas clients or selling through platforms often need to register sooner. Do I need separate GST registration for each state? Yes. Registration is state-wise. Premises in three states means three GSTINs on the same PAN.

GST registration is how a business gets its GST number from the government. Once registered, you can legally charge GST on sales, claim back the GST you paid on purchases, and trade across state lines without trouble.

Most businesses must register once yearly sales cross a set limit. Some must register from day one, no matter how small. And since 1 November 2025, many small businesses can get their number in three working days instead of waiting a week or more.
Here is everything you need: who must register, what papers to keep ready, how long it takes, what it costs, and what happens after your number arrives.
Think of it as getting a licence plate for your business in the tax system.
GST registration is the process. You fill out an online form, upload papers, and the department checks them.

paragraphs: GST registration is how a business gets its GST number from the government. Once registered, you can legally charge GST on sales, claim back the GST you paid on purchases, and trade across state lines without trouble.

Most businesses must register once yearly sales cross a set limit. Some must register from day one, no matter how small. And since 1 November 2025, many small businesses can get their number in three working days instead of waiting a week or more.
Here is everything you need: who must register, what papers to keep ready, how long it takes, what it costs, and what happens after your number arrives.
Think of it as getting a licence plate for your business in the tax system.
GST registration is the process. You fill out an online form, upload papers, and the department checks them.
GSTIN is what you get at the end: a 15-character Goods and Services Tax Identification Number, unique to you in that state.
Form GST REG-06 is your certificate. When someone asks for "proof of GST registration", this is what they mean.
Your GSTIN is state-specific. A shop in Delhi and a second in Haryana need two registrations. Same PAN, different GSTIN.
Registration number on that PAN in that state
So if a supplier's GSTIN starts with 09 but he claims to be in Mumbai, something is not right.
Two separate rules decide this. One looks at your sales. The other looks at what kind of business you run.
Cross the limit set for your state and supply type, and you must register. You get 30 days from the day you cross it, not 30 days from the end of the year.
Some businesses must register from the first rupee. This comes from Section 24 of the CGST Act.
Anyone supplying goods from one state to another
Casual taxable persons, such as a trader running a stall at a fair in another state
